articleTitle: An overview of sigma delta ADCs and DAC devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: Presents a review and intuitive introduction to oversampling DSP techniques and the theory and advantages of sigma delta (/spl Sigma/-/spl Delta/) devices for digital to analog conversion (DAC) and analogue to digital conversion (ADC). The paper initially introduces conventional Nyquist sampling rate DSP, followed by an overview of decimation, interpolation, and a discussion of the advantages of using oversampling to reduce the anti-alias and reconstruction filter specifications. It is then discussed why oversampling can be used to increase the resolution of an N-bit signal to N+1 bits, by sampling at 4/spl times/ the Nyquist rate to reduce the in-band ADC quantisation noise. Sigma-delta (/spl Sigma/-/spl Delta/) noise shaping techniques are then introduced and a brief overview of some devices is presented. Finally the authors comment on a few of the active research areas related to /spl Sigma/-/spl Delta/ devices.

articleTitle: A new architecture for bandpass sigma delta analogue to digital conversion
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: A new architecture for the implementation of bandpass sigma-delta A/D converters is described. The proposed architecture is hardware-efficient end has improved performance over existing topologies. A chopping scheme is used to shift signals from the passband to DC and a lowpass modulator used to perform the conversion. In the new implementation, the passband location is limited only by the maximum capacitor sampling rate possible, while in previous converters it was limited by the much slower integrator clock rate. Hence, the new converter can digitize bands at much higher frequencies than previous implementations. Simulation results are presented for a second-order modulator running at 1.07 MHz converting an input band at 10.7 MHz, a typical radio intermediate frequency.

articleTitle: Theory of lowpass and bandpass sigma-delta modulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: One-bit oversampled or sigma-delta analogue-to-digital conversion has been the subject of much research attention in recent years, finding use in a wide variety of applications. Theoretical analysis of this conversion method has been complicated by its nonlinear nature, precluding the application of standard linear circuit analysis methods. In recent years a number of researchers have undertaken a study of sigma-delta modulation based on nonlinear methods. This paper provides a summary of the results thus obtained, including results not previously published.

articleTitle: Non-linear deterministic dithering of sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: Sigma-delta modulators suffer from idle tone artefacts which degrade their linearity, even with high order modulation. The conventional linearization technique is to dither the quantizer with an external random noise source. Although successful, dither can be inefficient to implement and does not take advantage of certain properties of the one-bit quantizer. It has been shown that relatively linear modulator performance is inherently possible without the need for an external noise source, by modifying the quantizer operation with a nonlinear technique called bit-flipping. Two bit-dipping algorithms have been described, which enhance the linearity of the modulator. It has been shown that it is possible to linearize the modulator and reduce the quantization error power in the baseband, at the expense of increased hardware complexity. Both techniques are straightforward to implement and optimal performance is obtained by the choice of a single constant.

articleTitle: MASH structures for bandpass sigma-delta modulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: The paper presents simulation results from investigating the behaviour of multistage (MASH) oversampled bandpass sigma-delta (/spl Sigma/-/spl Delta/) modulators for use in analogue to digital converters for high frequency narrowband applications such as the signals out of the intermediate frequency (IF) section of a superheterodyne radio receiver. The bandpass configurations under consideration have in their loop filter a cascade of second-order resonator structures in order to achieve acceptable noise shaping. The quantisation noise in each stage is suppressed by feeding the error of each section into the input of the following stages. It is demonstrated that the triple effective-first-order bandpass MASH structure has significantly better performance compared with the effective-second-order effective-first-order bandpass MASH structure.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: The author discusses multistage modulators, digital processing of pulse density modulation signals, algorithms, testing, modeling nonidealities and stability. Diagrams are given for: an N/sup th/ order sigma delta modulator, a multistage closed loop modulator, a first order digital sigma delta modulator, and a low pass digital comb filter.

articleTitle: Implementing adaptive DSP algorithms using oversampled sigma delta strategies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: We present novel oversampled implementations of adaptive LMS FIR filters using sigma delta (/spl Sigma//spl Delta/) computation strategies. Using this approach in conjunction with /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ DACs and ADCs the need for expensive decimation and interpolation stages for the /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ codec has been circumvented. Hence the complete architecture can make considerable savings in total silicon area for a mixed signal ASIC implementation. The LMS algorithm performance of the /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ approach is shown to be comparable to the traditional Nyquist rate PCM LMS algorithm.

articleTitle: A single shot /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ architecture for multiplexed applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: This paper presents an alternative single shot /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ ADC architecture. The architecture is targeted at applications, such as industrial automation, where it is desirable to multiplex inputs from a number of independent sources. The "single shot" /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ does not require filter settling and so maximises the overall conversion rate for multiplexed applications. Results are presented for a fourth order /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ modulator which achieves 16 bit resolution with an oversampling rate of 200 samples per conversion. The circuit produces a new conversion every 350 microseconds.

articleTitle: Automatic generation of /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ D/A converter integrated circuits
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: A novel CAD tool for the design and automatic generation of /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ modulators for 1-bit /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ DACs is presented, Working from a user's specification the tool automates the modulator design subject to special stability criteria. The tool translates the design into VHDL. The generated VHDL is synthesized by commercial synthesis tools. The tool was used to design and generate a modulator for an 18-bit fifth-order /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ DAC.

articleTitle: Noise power estimation for poly-phase decimation filters: a frequency domain approach
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Oversampling and Sigma-Delta Strategies for DSP
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm used to calculate the total noise power for a specific decimation filter structure using a frequency domain approach. The assumed structure of the decimation filter is a cascade of double lowpass 2-path poly-phase blocks as presented by Kale, Morling and Krukowski (see IEE International Conference, ADDA '94, Cambridge, 6-8 July, 1994). To establish the validity of the frequency domain approach the algorithm has been incorporated into a program which determines the internal data-path widths required for a given output precision. Verification of the algorithm is then possible by performing fixed-point time domain simulations using the data-path widths suggested and estimating the total output noise power, Results of the noise power estimation algorithm and data-path width determination algorithm for a 7 stage decimation filter are reported.
